ai.seo_question: What is the condition for receiving God's specific mercy and good in this world and the Hereafter according to Surah Al-A'raf?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited in Shia supplications such as those in Sahifa Sajjadiyya, highlights the dialectic between divine justice and mercy, affirming that while punishment is selective, mercy is universal yet specifically realized through taqwa and charity. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the interplay between faith (iman), righteous action (amal), and divine grace, positioning the pious as the primary recipients of God's all-encompassing rahmah.

en.ahmedali: Enjoin for us good in the world, and good in the world to come. We turn to You alone."
And the Lord said: "I punish only those whom I will, but My mercy enfolds everything. I shall enjoin it for those who take heed for themselves, who pay the zakat and believe in My signs,
en.ahmedraza: “And destine good for us in this world and in the Hereafter – We have indeed inclined towards You”;
He said, “I give My punishment to whomever I will; and My mercy encompasses all things; so I shall soon destine favours for those who fear and pay the charity, and they believe in Our signs.”
en.arberry: And prescribe for us in this world good, and in the world to come; we have repented unto Thee.'

Said He, 'My chastisement -- I smite with it whom I will; and My mercy embraces all things, and I shall prescribe it for those who are godfearing and pay the alms, and those who indeed believe in Our signs,
en.daryabadi: And ordain for us good in the world and in the Hereafter; verily we have been guided unto Thee.

He said, “My punishment—I inflict it upon whomever I will, but My mercy encompasses all things. I will specify it for those who act righteously and practice regular charity, and those who believe in Our signs.”
